audit.summary: An exact permitted Q3 complementary-series example produces an uncancelled double pole on an allowed Theorem2(1) contour. Theorem2(2) omits its diagonal exclusion. Selected normalization, changes of variables, global residue algebra and application manipulations checked correctly; no general failure of the spectral strategy asserted.
limitations: P001 — Theorem 2(1)'s advertised forward contour strip and holomorphy assertion — Counterevidence: Keeping the contour above θ1+θ2, as in Theorem 1, avoids this explicit pole. To use that strip non-vacuously also requires the corresponding nonempty-strip inequality. This is a verified restriction for the example and consistent with the source's derivation; it is not a new certification of every case of a repaired theorem. Alternatively, an explicit normalization of the inducing character and a justified continuation argument would need to be stated and proved. The checked Jacobian and character factors themselves are correct, and this finding does not establish failure of the whole transform strategy, its tempered cases, or the global results.

P002 — Theorem 2(2) omits the diagonal exclusion or an explicit extension convention — Counterevidence: The off-diagonal formula's factors match the change of variables. H itself supplies a smooth diagonal extension.

proposition.claim:
For all θ1<σ<1/2−θ, the forward χ-integral is absolutely convergent and its χ-integrand is holomorphic in θ1<Re(χ)<1/2−θ.

F=Q3 and ψ has conductor Z3. The self-dual additive measure has vol(Z3)=1; d×y=dy/|y|. π1=π=I(1) are irreducible generic tempered unramified principal series of PGL2(Q3). Set θ1=θ=0. π2=I(|.|^(−1/4)) is an irreducible unitarizable generic complementary principal series, with θ2=1/4. The source permits I(χ2) for some character and imposes no Re(χ2)≥0 condition in its setup. Take χ2=|.|^(−1/4), χ0=1, W1(a(u))=1_(1+3Z3)(u), and W2(a(u))=1_(2+3Z3)(u). These functions are real, so the conjugations visible in the source do not alter this test. The proposed vectors may be constructed directly from (2.9)-(2.10): on the open Bruhat cell take f_j(wn(x))=(1/3)ψ(a_j x)1_(3^(−1)Z3)(x), with a_1=1,a_2=2, and inducing characters 1 and |.|^(−1/4), respectively. A compactly supported smooth section on that cell extends by zero to the induced model. Fourier inversion gives the stated unit-coset restrictions, since the factors |u|^(1/2)χ_j(u)^(−1) equal 1 on their supports. The hypotheses of Theorem 1 also hold for this example because θ1+θ2+θ=1/4<1/2. With target π tempered and χ0 unitary, the D=1 decay assertion in Lemma 2.6 gives absolute convergence of the defining h-sharp integral.

The formula is quantified for y∈F×, including y=1.

y=1 is allowed by the printed quantifier.
